contexts.text: To ride upon the word of truth () = to teach the doctrine of truth. ( = the intelligence of truth... AC 2761:6.)
To ride in chariot and on horses () = an abundance of intellectual things.
Chariots and horsemen = principles of falsity.
Horsemen = those who state truth.
A rider = one who is intelligent.
His rider (who falls backward) () = one who teaches.
To ride on the clouds () = the understanding of the Word as to its interiors.
Jehovah riding upon a cherub () = the Providence of the Lord lest man should enter from himself into the mysteries of faith which are in the Word.
To ride upon a chariot, and upon horses () = to be instructed in the doctrine of truth from the Word with internal understanding. AC 5044:8.
To ride upon the high places of the earth () = intelligence. AE 314:7, Explained. AE 617:14, Explained.
I will smite... his rider with madness () = one who is intelligent struck with madness. AE 355:6, Explained.
To ride upon a donkey was a sign that the Natural had been subordinated; and to ride on a foal the son of a she-donkey, that the Rational had been subordinated.
They rode upon camels () = the Intellectual elevated above natural scientifics.
That he is then withdrawn from truth, is signified by his rider falling backward. AC 6401, Explained.
To ride is predicated of Ephraim, because to ride is to enjoy understanding...
Horsemen () = intellectual things. Illustrated.
He made them ride upon a donkey () = things of service to the new intelligence. To ride = the things which are of the understanding... because a horse = the Intellectual.
Thy walls shall shake at the noise of the horsemen ()... Horsemen = the things of a perverted Intellectual.
Horsemen = the things which are of the understanding; here, the horsemen of Pharaoh, false reasonings from a perverted Intellectual. AC 8188:end. AC 8210. AC 8265. AC 8332.
The horse and his rider hath He cast into the sea () = at His presence the falsities of faith and evils of life have cast themselves into Hell. Horse and rider = falsities from evil.
Horsemen who run () = reasoners.
Elijah and Elisha were called... the horsemen of Israel () because both represented the Lord as to the Word; and by... horsemen is signified intelligence.
Horsemen = intelligence. AE 355:12.
Horseman = wisdom thence.

By horsemen () are signified reasonings about faith alone, because by a horse is signified the understanding of the Word destroyed; hence horsemen = reasonings from the understanding of the Word destroyed... AE 573.
His rider () = the lack of knowledge from them, by which truths are perverted. ( = ratiocination from these. AE 355:8.)
A ludicrous cavalry seen, Described, Explained.
I saw four horsemen as it were flying out of a cloud. Described, Explained.
To ride = to instruct in Divine truths from the Word. Illustrated.
To ride upon horses () = to persuade from the fallacies of the senses, and through reasonings thence.
To ride upon horses () = that the Lord is in the understanding of His Word in its spiritual sense.
Rider = the affection of spiritual truth whence is understanding.
To ride = to give intelligence and wisdom. Illustrated.
The voice of the horseman = ratiocination... AE 411:19.
Horsemen, etc. = assaults on truth... good. AE 355:23.
To ride upon a horse = ratiocination. AE 355:30.
To ride upon white donkeys = perception of good.
Horsemen = ratiocinations. AE 654:42. AE 654:45.
To ride upon horses, when predicated of the Lord, = the Divine wisdom which is in the Word.
To ride = to give understanding and to illustrate.
Horsemen = the intelligent.
To make a man ride on our head () = no intelligence.
Horseman = intelligence.
To ride, when predicated of the Lord, = to illustrate the understanding. AE 594:5. AE 594:6. AE 594:7.
To ride = to instruct and combat.
Horsemen = heresies.
